channel.description: Latest articles from Carolinas' Own Queen City News WJZY-TV (fox46.com)

item.title: Rain expected to return Thursday, sunny weekend ahead
item.description: Temperatures warmed up on Wednesday, with rain and cooler weather expected to return early next week and a sunny weekend ahead.

item.title: CATS riders react to new text tipline for concerns
item.description: Passengers on Charlotte Area Transit System trains and buses can now report issues by texting a tipline, in response to a recent murder on the blue line that was referenced in President Trump's State of the Union address.

item.title: Fort Mill leaders add off-duty officers to help reduce traffic in school zones
item.description: Fort Mill School District and town officials are taking proactive measures to reduce traffic and improve safety around schools, including adding off-duty officers and installing a traffic light at Catawba Ridge High School.

item.title: Waymo preparing to launch driverless ride‑hailing service in Charlotte
item.description: Waymo has driven more than 200 million miles fully autonomously and has provided more than 20 million such rides.

item.title: Alleged predatory towing controversy at a Bojangles near South End
item.description: A man was allegedly towed and charged $750 for a car that was booted while he was in the Bojangles restaurant bathroom, but Bojangles corporate reimbursed him and said the towing company did not have permission to tow from the property.

item.title: Four taken into ICE custody at Mecklenburg County Courthouse
item.description: Four people were taken into ICE custody at the Mecklenburg County Courthouse, and ICE agents threatened to arrest three attorneys for attempting to interfere with the arrests.

item.title: Federal lawsuit filed over warrantless arrests during Charlotte immigration sweeps
item.description: CHARLOTTE (QUEEN CITY NEWS) -- A group representing several U.S. citizens arrested during immigration sweeps in North Carolina is now taking legal action against the United States Department of Homeland Security. item.title: Two injured in southwest Charlotte house fire
item.description: Two people were injured in a house fire in southwest Charlotte Wednesday night, with one person taken to an area hospital with minor injuries and the second person being treated for serious injuries but is stable.
